P4.detail: [UNSPECIFIED] Conviction motion: `02` §5.5 says convictions move 'slowly, by scar and crisis'  @Person[saemund].convictions[Faith]  needs: a scar object, an owner, a write class, and a crisis rule

P8.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] feud inheritance: nothing at death writes the deceased's stances into a kinsman's interior, and claim confidence decays — so an enmity is LOST BY BEING FORGOTTEN  @P8 inheritance  needs: a WITNESS/CENSUS rule depositing high-weight stances into kin ledgers

P11.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] conflicting obligation: two `oblige` Tenures may coexist and nothing computes that satisfying one breaches the other; the collision rule is specified for Propositions (`02` §3, intersecting `when`), not for obligations  @P11 dual loyalty  needs: an obligation-collision Query, or oblige carrying a Proposition it discharges

P12.detail: OK: progress 1.0 -> 0.0. A stranger obstructed Maret with no `obstruct` verb, no knowledge of her, and no resolver branch — derived-at-read does the work

F2.detail: [UNSPECIFIED] `leaders()` comparator — `02` §10 item 2 proposes 'commitment degree x backing raisable', unadopted  @leaders(rm,realm)  needs: a comparator; and it must read `succeed` edges before it (see FINDINGS §2.8)

F6.detail: [UNSPECIFIED] the judging set's decision rule at a sitting — `02` §2.2 names `judging_set_rule` as a Rung field and no document specifies its form or how a motion is carried  @F6 sitting decision  needs: a specified decision rule; the archive has ten motion types and two vote models

W1.doc: a site decays until a verb leaves its option set

W2.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] band strobing: 7 crossing events in 6 seasons at the tending equilibrium. W3.detail: OK: wear fires at MATTER with no actor; the world churns with nobody in it

W4.detail: [FORBIDDEN] an agentive actorless row — 'an empire demands a levy' is an actor's decision rendered as weather. `05` §4.4 blocks it until a criterion exists that stops any actor being reclassified as weather  @W4 off-board agency  needs: the agentive/non-agentive criterion, or a simulated foreign person

A1.doc: an arc ENDS at a sitting somebody convenes

A2.detail: [FORBIDDEN] an Event writing social row (Office, post)  @Office.post  needs: an Act by a person

A3.doc: an arc turns on the state of the world-substrate

A4.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] provenance: `resolve` emits Events with an EMPTY causes[] — nothing in the specified loop populates the causal edge that `06` §1 calls the arc itself  @A4 provenance chain  needs: resolve() to attribute each Event to the claims/events that motivated its act
A4.doc: a story is recoverable by walking causes[] backwards

A5.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] boundedness: grievance rose monotonically to 9 over 8 seasons with nothing damping it. Per-tick emission caps bound a cascade WITHIN a season; nothing bounds a behavioural spiral ACROSS seasons, and no guard or measurement is licensed for it  @A5 termination  needs: a termination argument per self-feeding mechanism + a sustained-shock battery
A5.doc: a self-reinforcing loop runs and provably terminates

A6.detail: OK: legitimacy is a Query over claims, so it flips per-knower at telling speed
A6.doc: a secret becomes public and legitimacy collapses retroactively

P13.detail: OK: presence is a `contain` Tenure; travel is an act; travel-in-progress ticks at MATTER
P13.doc: a person is somewhere, and moving costs something

P14.detail: [UNSPECIFIED] (Person, capability) has no row in the Partition schema  @Person.capability  needs: a social: bool column entry
P14.doc: a person gets better at something

P15.detail: [COLLISION] marriage: `01` Law 4 names marriage as a governed social change, but no Tenure kind carries it — `tie` is an affective bond that DECAYS, and a dynastic marriage is a durable political instrument that binds two houses and routes succession  @P15 marriage  needs: marriage as an `oblige`-class Tenure with a payload, or an eighth kind
P15.doc: two people marry, and the bond is a political fact

P16.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] subsistence: `02` §8.1 says subsistence happens TO a person at MATTER, but no step consumes stores on their behalf and no rule links a person to a larder — so `need` in `Sensation` has no producer either  @P16 subsistence  needs: a MATTER draw per contained person against the Rung's stores
P16.doc: a person without a post feeds themselves

P17.detail: [UNSPECIFIED] individuation: `05` row 13 requires the world to mint a Person on demand with no decider, and no rule says WHAT TRIGGERS IT or what interior the new person starts with — `02` §10 item 3 carries the 'plausible past' as open and ruled-against in three placements  @P17 individuation  needs: a trigger condition and a specified starting interior for a minted person
P17.doc: the world produces the person a situation requires

A7.detail: OK: an institution acts through a named person at a venue; 'the Church acted' is a reading of the log, never a row in it
A7.doc: an institution acts as one body

A8.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] the lapse: `05` §5.1 calls a date passing unheard 'a real consequence' with 'nobody's act, nobody to blame' — but nothing EMITS it, so the specific injury of being ignored is not witnessable and cannot enter anyone's ledger  @A8 lapse  needs: CALENDAR to emit a lapse Event for a date that fired with no answering act
A8.doc: a deadline passes with nothing heard, and that is itself the consequence

A9.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] no step decrements a Record's ttl. `05` rows 11a/11b make a ttl expiry and an act-created term's ripening the carriers for cooldowns, remissions and truces — and MATTER never touches them  @A9 ttl  needs: a MATTER pass over Records decrementing ttl and emitting expiry
A9.doc: a term ripens and a truce runs out

A10.detail: [UNSPECIFIED] vacancy-by-absence: `06` row 3 requires a convening condition to read PRESENCE, so that making a man absent substitutes for killing him — `ConveningCondition` is a six-field object the adversarial pass found had no owner, and its predicate form is unspecified  @A10 hostage politics  needs: a specified ConveningCondition predicate that can read a person's address
A10.doc: a person is removed from play without being killed

A11.detail: OK-BUT: the claim persists (a Proposition is immutable) and each pressing is an act, but the only accumulator is other people's claims, which decay under the universal rule — so a long campaign of pressing is not distinguishable from a recent one except by re-reading the log
A11.doc: something ripens over many seasons and pays off late

A12.detail: OK — death ends the tenure and a storm cannot. The seam `05` §7 leaves open is CLOSED by `02` §5.1, and it is closed by a causation rule rather than by the column
A12.doc: a person is killed, and their tenures end — and a storm may NOT do the same

P18.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] staged institutional judgement: a stage computed as a Query over current stances REVERTS the moment the stances do, so an army that has decided its king is unfit un-decides it after one good season. A ratchet needs state that survives its inputs, and Law 3 forbids exactly that state  @P18 loyalty stages  needs: either a per-person scar/ratchet the Query reads (see P4), or an explicit exception to Law 3 for monotone institutional judgement
P18.doc: an institution reassesses its loyalty in STAGES that do not revert on their own

P19.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] deferral: a person who chooses nothing produces no Act, so no Event, so nothing enters anyone's ledger — a ruler's sustained refusal to decide is INVISIBLE to the world and indistinguishable from his absence  @P19 inaction  needs: an abstention that emits, so that not-deciding is witnessable and chargeable
P19.doc: not acting is itself a choice, and costs something

P20.detail: OK: dispatch names one person who runs their own choose, so the deed done is the subordinate's, not the holder's — and the holder learns of it only by witnessing
P20.doc: an order is carried out differently from how it was intended

P21.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] publicness: the same act by a king and by a copyist produces Events identical in scope and witnessability. Nothing in Act, Event or witness() reads the actor's office, so office cannot make an act cost more — and `07` §5 asks precisely that it do so  @P21 visibility cost  needs: a witnessability term keyed on the actor's standing/office, not on the act
P21.doc: high office is MORE constrained by visibility than a private person

P22.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] privacy: WITNESS as specified fans every Event out to every person, so there is no private utterance — a councillor's frank advice is heard by the whole realm. `06` §4.2 names five witness CHANNELS as the cast gate, but the loop never consults them  @P22 private vs public  needs: witness() to consult presence/channel before depositing, not after
P22.doc: the same words cost differently said in private and in public

P23.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] act cooldown: the claim was pressed 3 seasons running with no cost and no bar. `05` §4.1 gives event ROWS a required cooldown; nothing gives an ACT one, so a failed bid for a throne is a free repeatable check rather than a bet  @P23 act cooldown  needs: a per-act-kind cooldown carried by the actor, or a Record with a ttl that gates eligibility (the shape already has the Record; nothing writes it here)
P23.doc: a failed attempt costs standing and cannot be retried for some seasons

P24.detail: OK-BUT: the acts resolve and the office declares its revocation basis, but WHETHER THE MOTION CARRIES is the unspecified judging-set rule of F6 — so revocation reaches the venue and stops there
P24.doc: a collective body revokes the authority it granted

P25.detail: OK: the operative's own choose returns a weaker act; her divided stance is her interior and nobody may read it — investigating is the only route, which is the design
P25.doc: a subordinate silently underperforms, and nobody can tell without investigating

P26.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] accumulation vs decay: Edeyja holds 6 claims of harm, but the only accumulator the shape offers is a ledger whose confidence DECAYS and whose rows are EVICTED at a cap. A threshold over 'visible harm accumulated' is therefore a race between witnessing and forgetting, and the shape has no counter that only goes up  @P26 accumulation  needs: a monotone per-person tally (the archive's scar is exactly this shape), or an explicit statement that patience is a Query over undecayed claims and is losable
P26.doc: accumulated visible harm crosses a threshold and forces a confrontation

P27.detail: [UNSPECIFIED] contested formation: investments in a person resolve as Events he witnesses, but nothing converts accumulated tutoring into a DURABLE alignment, and nothing closes a window after which it LOCKS. `02` §10 item 3 carries the 'plausible past' of a newly made person as open; this is the same hole seen from the other end — how a person's interior is FORMED  @P27 formation window  needs: a specified route from repeated acts upon a person to that person's convictions (which is P4's missing mechanism again), plus a lock condition
P27.doc: a contested person's allegiance is won by investment inside a closing window

P28.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] craft: `02` §7.4 has `Record` — the only non-person root-bearer, keepable at a Rung, burnable, admissible at a venue — which is exactly the object a copyist makes. But no act CREATES one: `resolve` emits Events and nothing mints a Record, so the shape has the noun and not the verb  @P28 making a thing  needs: a `create`-mode StateChange whose subject is a Record, produced by an act
P28.doc: a person MAKES a durable object that outlives the scene

P29.detail: [COLLISION] possession: a Record is homed as Rung matter, so it is at a PLACE and never in a person's hands — 'she was found with it' is not expressible, and possession-as-offence has no subject. P10 found the same hole from the custody side; they are one gap  @P29 possession  needs: a person-to-Record `hold` Tenure, which also closes P10
P29.doc: merely HOLDING a thing is actionable against you

P30.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] work-in-progress: `02` §8.1 names travel-in-progress as ticking at MATTER, but there is no general partial-work record, so every act completes or fails within its season. A craft, a school, a survey or a long investigation cannot be half-done and interrupted  @P30 ongoing work  needs: an act that deposits a Record with remaining effort, which MATTER advances
P30.doc: work spans seasons and can be interrupted partway

P31.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] environmental cost: a person contained at a Rung whose Site is derelict takes NOTHING from it. MATTER wears Sites; nothing wears the PEOPLE standing next to them, so a Warden's thirty-one years of proximity to substrate damage is free  @P31 proximity harm  needs: a MATTER pass from Site condition onto contained persons — the same shape as subsistence (P16), which is also missing
P31.doc: a person is worn down by WHERE THEY ARE, not by what they do

P32.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] sacrifice: `resolve` reads no stake from an Act, so spending your life on an act cannot buy a different outcome than performing it and living. Orm's death-seal and an ordinary seal are the same Event  @P32 self-sacrifice  needs: a declared stake on an Act that the resolver may read, priced against the ladder
P32.doc: spending your life on an act buys something a surviving act cannot

P33.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] two standings: `Sensation.standing` is a single scalar defined as what EVERYONE reads off you, so a reputation held only among people who can never publicly credit you has no carrier — and a covert operative's whole economy is that second, unreadable standing  @P33 covert standing  needs: standing as a Query over a NAMED audience, not a global scalar
P33.doc: one person carries two independent standings that move separately

A13.detail: [FORBIDDEN] an Event writing social row (Person, stance)  @Person.stance  needs: an Act by a person
A13.doc: an ambient SOCIAL quantity drifts from the ABSENCE of anyone acting

A14.detail: [UNSPECIFIED] (Person, capability) has no row in the Partition schema  @Person.capability  needs: a social: bool column entry

A15.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] reserve: nothing marks an act as once-per-arc, nothing records that it is being WITHHELD, and nothing lets its value decay while unused. Holding a hammer is indistinguishable from not having one (and see P19 — the holding itself emits nothing)  @A15 held reserve  needs: an act kind with a use-once flag and a value that varies with world state, so that waiting is a priced decision rather than an absence
A15.doc: a once-per-arc resource is held in reserve, and the window can close unannounced

A16.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] procedural advance: an accusation, a probate, a licence application — a process with STAGES that advance on their own timetable — has no carrier. A Record is inert (A9 shows even its ttl is never decremented), and CALENDAR fires dates rather than advancing processes. So a case against you cannot ripen while you do nothing  @A16 procedural stages  needs: a staged Record that MATTER advances, whose stage gates what acts are available
A16.doc: a formal process advances on its own stages regardless of anyone acting

A17.detail: OK: the two are separate acts by separate persons in separate seasons, and the second can fail on its own — the shape gets this right for free, because a Dispensation is published as a telling and compliance is each hearer's own choose
A17.doc: winning the argument and enforcing the win are SEPARATE events, and the second can fail

A18.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] persistent condition: an Event is a fact in the log, not a state on a thing. Nothing carries 'this unit is stuck', 'this person is disgraced', 'this place is under interdict' — a condition that outlives its scene and gates later acts. `09`'s seam returns Events from a contest and stops there  @A18 lingering condition  needs: a condition Record attached to a carrier, with a clearing act — the same shape A16 and P30 need, which is one gap seen three ways
A18.doc: a rare roll leaves a condition that outlives the scene that produced it

A19.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] loss of agency: the loop hands EVERY person in `world.persons` to `choose`. There is no state in which a person exists, is lucid, and may no longer choose — so an irreversible personal floor cannot be represented, and the arc that exists BECAUSE the rule has no exit has no rule  @A19 irreversible floor  needs: a per-person agency predicate the DELIBERATE map consults, and an act class that can cross it one way only
A19.doc: a person crosses an irreversible personal floor and stops being an agent

P34.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] self-accumulating hidden exposure: the duke performed 5 ordinary acts and the shape retains them ONLY as Events in the world log and as decaying Claims in whoever witnessed them. There is no per-person quantity that (a) climbs from the person's own acts, (b) is NOT readable by that person, and (c) can fire. The nearest thing, the claim ledger, is the wrong shape three ways over: it is other people's, it decays, and its holder reads it  @P34 hidden self-accumulation  needs: a monotone interior counter fed by the actor's OWN acts at WITNESS, excluded from that person's own View, with a firing rule that produces an Act by SOMEONE ELSE rather than an outcome — otherwise it is A2's forbidden threshold wearing a hat
P34.doc: a quantity accumulates in a person from their OWN ordinary acts, unknown to them

P35.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] contested quantity: both acts resolved and emitted ['restore', 'wreck']; the site's condition took both deltas independently. That is correct for matter and it is NOT contest — nothing in `resolve()` sees that two acts addressed one target in one season, so there is no net, no opposition, and no way for a blocker to hold a line  @P35 opposed acts on one target  needs: either an explicit statement that opposition is emergent from summed deltas and arcs must be written that way, or a resolve() that groups acts by target — the second is a second resolver and the shape's own meta-rule forbids it
P35.doc: an actor is stopped by an opponent building the SAME quantity in the same place

P36.detail: [NO-PRODUCER] action budget: `choose(Person, View, Sensation) -> Act` returns ONE Act, and DELIBERATE called it 1 time(s). A season is one act per person, so nobody triages, nothing is left undone, and a King's scarcity is identical to a copyist's. Note what this also voids: `14` closes the petition-spray defect 'PROVISIONALLY by one act per person', a fix that does not survive the stated player model of ~5  @P36 acts per season  needs: `choose` returning an ORDERED Act[] bounded by a per-person budget, with the budget itself a Query (office, condition, distance travelled) rather than a constant — and a re-answer to petition-spray that survives a budget above one
P36.doc: a person gets ~5 acts in a season and must choose which pressures to leave unaddressed

ARC-01.name: The Unworked Clause
ARC-01.one_line: Two rulers' independently-rational refusals to act compound, through a background cultural-drift track neither is watching, into a forced crisis nobody chose.
ARC-01.ends_when: when either the background cultural track bottoms out in a Crown territory (forcing an Emergence crisis with unspecified content) or players remove one named cost-component of the Sovereign Constraint, enabling Almud to act at a lower difficulty — a threshold crossing forces the choice; it is not scheduled, and neither actor's own restraint contains a mechanism to end it unassisted.
who_acts: King Almud (Crown) — whether to act, once a threshold forces the question; his private ethical doubt is his own to resolve or not
Confessor Himlensendt (Church) — does not decide to create the crisis; his accumulation is passive/unconscious
players — may choose to remove one specific cost from Almud's calculus
UNCLEAR: nobody is named as deciding when the background cultural track itself resolves — it is explicitly passive drift

rows.need: a background/ambient quantity tied to a population's cultural situation must be able to drift toward a pole purely from the absence of any faction's action in its territories, with no faction action driving the drift

a person's genuinely unresolved private ethical question (not a secret sympathy, not a settled belief) must be able to function as a real, load-bearing reason for a leader's inaction, distinct from and alongside the named external costs of acting

one actor's accumulation of institutional standing must be able to happen through methods that are individually unimpeachable (charity, arbitration, hospitals) with no single action anyone could point to as the trigger for concern
a Non-Player Character must be able to accumulate an effect at scale while having zero perceptual capacity to register what that accumulation produces elsewhere

players must be able to remove one specific named cost-component from a leader's decision calculus as a discrete, resolvable action, after which that leader's prior refusal to act converts into willingness

when a background track bottoms out in a territory, the system must be able to force a previously-open, never-stated question into a concrete binary position, with the forcing coming from the track itself rather than from any actor choosing to force it
UNCLEAR: what mechanically happens once the background track's floor triggers 'Restoration Movement Emergence' is not specified — the source calls this 'latent faction mechanics, pending design'

ARC-02.name: The Unseeing Eye
ARC-02.one_line: A Church scholar's ordinary, individually-defensible institutional placement causes him to spontaneously develop a sensitivity the institution has no way to see coming or notice once it starts.
ARC-02.ends_when: when the growth check succeeds and the resulting trajectory (three divergent outcomes) resolves — either through a player's disclosure prompting the character's own informed choice, or, absent disclosure, through an unnamed GM-judgment resolution of the character's belief structure; the triggering check's firing season is itself stochastic (as early as the first sustained exposure, as late as several seasons on), so there is no scheduled or counter-driven end.
who_acts: Cardinal Klapp — his eventual trajectory, if given information to choose with
players — whether and when to disclose what they perceive about him
UNCLEAR: nobody in-world is named as deciding Klapp's trajectory if players do not tell him — it 'fires' via GM judgment, not a named actor's choice

rows.need: an institution's routine, individually-defensible placement decisions must be able to compound, over years, into an outcome that harms one of its own members, without any single decision-maker choosing that outcome or being positioned to see it coming

a character must be able to change in a way that is invisible to himself but perceptible to a third party with a specific trained sense, creating a gap between what an observer can see about a person and what that person knows about himself

a slow-accumulating exposure quantity tied to routine, unremarkable activity must be able to build up over multiple seasons purely from someone doing their normal job, with no single operation classifiable as 'the risky one'
a spontaneous state-change check on a person must be able to fire without any actor — including that person — initiating it or being aware a check is occurring

an institution must be able to hold a standing response protocol for a condition that nonetheless fails to trigger against one specific member, because nobody is watching for the precondition in that member's particular case

a third party must be able to choose, as a discrete scene, to disclose a hidden fact about a person's own condition to that person, with the person's subsequent trajectory depending on whether they were told

UNCLEAR: which of several divergent personal trajectories a character takes when NOT given the information is not governed by a named mechanism — the source says it 'fires according to Klapp's Belief structure,' resolved by GM judgment from prior scene evidence, not by a defined roll or deciding actor
one person's individual capability shift (being reassigned or leaving) must be able to reduce an institution's aggregate operational capacity as a downstream, mechanical consequence

ARC-03.name: The Hammer's Reserve
ARC-03.one_line: A leader holds a single decisive, non-repeatable resource in reserve for the perfect moment, while two separate accumulating threats she isn't tracking together close the window she's waiting for.
ARC-03.ends_when: when the reserved resource is finally used — triggered by one of three non-exclusive paths: players hand the holder a nameable pretext (a choice), an unrelated event trips the rival counter forcing her hand (nobody decides), or the counter's approach to its own threshold overrides her patience via her own Beliefs (a forced self-decision). It never ends on a calendar date, and the 'correct' timing window can close before any of the three paths fires.
who_acts: Duchess Baralta — whether and when to fire the reserved resource; her private judgment of 'the moment' is not externally legible
Ehrenwall (rival faction) — counts, but its counting is blind to Baralta's own reasoning
players — may supply the pretext she is waiting for

rows.need: a single named decisive resource (usable once per arc) must be able to be held in reserve across multiple seasons purely by its holder's own judgment that using it later beats using it now

two independent counters (one faction's rising standing, an unrelated coup-threat counter) must be able to accumulate on separate clocks not visibly linked to each other, such that a character optimizing against one can be blindsided by the other
a reserved resource's effectiveness must be able to have a real, GM-judged optimal timing window that can close without any explicit in-fiction signal announcing that it has closed
players must be able to supply the specific target or pretext a holding character is waiting for, as an action distinct from triggering the reserved resource itself
an unrelated faction's threat-counter must be able to increment based on the ABSENCE of a rival's action in a season, not on any action taken

a character's own ethical commitments must be able to force her to use a reserved resource once a threshold is crossed, independent of and potentially overriding her stated strategic judgment about optimal timing

firing a reserved resource must be able to produce categorically different outcomes, not just different magnitudes, depending on whether a separate threshold was already crossed at the moment of firing

ARC-04.name: Vaynard's Wager
ARC-04.one_line: A leader's deliberate strategic non-commitment toward a subordinate collides with a formal accusation process that advances on its own procedural timetable regardless of his inaction.
ARC-04.ends_when: when the patron is forced to choose publicly among defend/abandon/extract, after the subordinate loses a formal contest against the accusing institution — a forcing event produced by the accusation process's own procedural stages advancing on schedule, not by the patron's continued deferral; the arc cannot end merely by the patron continuing to withhold a decision.
who_acts: Duke Vaynard — the forced choice among defend/abandon/extract, when it finally arrives
Maret Uln — whether to continue the research, and (via a contest) whether he prevails against the Inquisitors
the Inquisitors/Church — advance procedurally regardless of Vaynard's inaction
players — can affect the contest's odds or attempt extraction

rows.need: a Non-Player Character must be able to sustain deliberate, ongoing non-commitment toward a subordinate (neither supporting nor suppressing them) as a real strategic stance across multiple seasons, with that stance itself imposing no immediate mechanical cost
a subordinate's trust/loyalty in a patron must be able to erode from that patron's inaction alone, on a track with no mechanic to actively increase it — an asymmetric, one-directional gauge

ARC-R17.name: The Favour Gate
ARC-R17.one_line: A diffuse, non-unified economic actor must be persuadable only piecemeal, in a specific place, under time pressure from an opposing actor undoing the same work.
ARC-R17.ends_when: the leverage action is executed (successfully or not) against the chosen target, or the players abandon the approach
who_acts: the players
the diffuse economic faction (acting differently per location)
the opposing institutional faction running counter-actions
an individual officer within the diffuse faction (fallback path)

rows.need: a faction that is not a single decision-maker must have its allegiance/capacity be a per-location quantity rather than one faction-wide value
building a local quantity toward a use-threshold must be contestable by an opposing actor's action in the same location and window, with a net effect that can be zero or negative
reaching a threshold quantity in one place must unlock a specific powerful action usable against a chosen target elsewhere
an opposing actor must be able to detect a pattern of investment and redirect its own effort specifically to counter it there
there must be an alternate, narrower route to a partial version of the same capability, through an individual person rather than the whole diffuse actor
gains and losses to the same quantity in a period must be bounded so no single action fully solves the problem in one go

ARC-R18.name: The Tied Vote
ARC-R18.one_line: [STRUCK-MECHANIC: Coup Counter] A formal collective-decision procedure between two evenly matched sides must be able to end in a tie, with background trend-quantities moving against everyone simultaneously and a third party's private tally quietly advancing.
ARC-R18.ends_when: the vote resolves (clean win, clean loss, or tie) -- a single formal sitting with a definite convened moment, not an open-ended condition
who_acts: Crown/Hafenmark (side calling or supporting the vote)
the Church (opposing side)
third-party factions being whipped for votes
an outside observer tracking a private tally toward a future intervention

rows.need: a multi-round formal vote between two competing coalitions must be able to end with neither side reaching the majority needed to prevail
a tied/failed formal vote must trigger two independent background quantities to move in the same negative direction simultaneously, regardless of what either side wanted
pre-vote persuasion of a third party's allegiance must require advance investment before the vote is called, wasted if a competing actor persuades the same party back
the side that called the vote must not always have the foreknowledge advantage -- the opposing side may know a vote is coming first
a repeat vote on the same matter must not be immediately available -- some interval must pass, allowing background processes to advance in the gap
a failing outcome must visibly change how a watching third-party actor advances a separate, private running tally toward a future intervention

ARC-R19.name: The Accounting Sequence
ARC-R19.one_line: A strict, unchangeable phase order for resolving pending effects each period must let timing of an intervention matter more than its content, and personal-scale actions must sometimes reach further than the actor realizes.
ARC-R19.ends_when: never, as an ongoing structural mechanism; as a focal arc it concludes at the accounting where two simultaneously-threatened factions' checks resolve and the triage choice takes effect
who_acts: the players (choosing where to spend limited actions)
each pressured faction (whose checks fire automatically in a fixed phase)
third-party factions reinterpreting an action as hostile

rows.need: periodic resolution of pending effects must happen in a fixed, non-negotiable phase order, such that an effect resolved in an early phase can prevent a check that would otherwise fire later in the same period, but not vice versa
when an at-risk quantity drops to a specific low value, that value must impose a protective floor on further pressure for a limited grace window, independent of the pressure's true magnitude
gains or losses to a single quantity from any number of separate actions in one period must be bounded to a fixed maximum
helping one at-risk holder in a period must be able to consume the same limited capacity that would otherwise have protected a different, simultaneously at-risk holder
an action taken to help one actor must be interpretable by a third, unrelated actor as hostile, generating a fresh pressure against a target the acting player did not intend to provoke
an action taken by a player at a small, personal scale must be able to silently register as also affecting a faction-scale quantity, invisible until the periodic accounting is read

ARC-20.name: The Tutoring Demand
ARC-20.one_line: [STRUCK-MECHANIC: Coup Counter] A rising background pressure must reach a threshold and force a binary demand, whose two response paths open independent decaying-loyalty and accelerating-pressure tracks that eventually converge on a battle a specific commander decides, alone, whether to fight.
ARC-20.ends_when: never as a single event -- Branch A resolves when the sent heir's status locks in (recovered, extracted, or lost) or Branch B resolves when the invasion battle concludes; both branches hand off into further political consequence
who_acts: the ruling monarch (choosing comply/refuse/delay each period)
the sent heir (whose internal allegiance shifts over time)
his sibling embedded abroad (deciding whether/how to intervene)
the covert intelligence apparatus (maintaining contact at risk of exposure)
the opposing empire (deploying forces once thresholds are crossed)
an economic faction (deciding when self-interest outweighs loyalty)
the military leader (deciding whether to commit forces)

rows.need: a slowly rising background pressure quantity must, on crossing a threshold, force a formal binary demand on the ruling actor with no third option other than delay at increasing cost

a person sent away as the compliant response must have a decaying allegiance value that ticks down every period unless someone spends effort maintaining it, with a floor beneath which the decay becomes irreversible
a person embedded inside the opposing power must be reachable only through a costly, uncertain action, and must be able to slow but not fully reverse the decaying allegiance above
the sent person's allegiance hitting its floor must trigger an irreversible state change that itself forces a specific costly response (military action) rather than further diplomacy

the refusal path's accelerating pressure must feed a trade dependency that an unrelated economic faction notices and can eventually turn against the refusing side out of its own self-interest, not because it was ordered to

the eventual mass-combat event's outcome must depend on whether one specific, independently-judging military leader decides to commit her forces, and that decision must be resolvable in more than one way even under identical battlefield facts

ARC-21.name: The Excommunication
ARC-21.one_line: A single formal judicial contest between an institution and an individual power-holder must resolve to one of several qualitatively different outcome tiers, each removing or strengthening a suppression effect on a separate rising background pressure.
ARC-21.ends_when: the immediate consequence cascade from the single roll stabilizes (seizure halted or completed, or the institution's own counter-collapse addressed) -- branch-dependent, not a universal endpoint
who_acts: the institution's chief prosecutor
the institution's overall head (torn between doctrine and consequence)
the accused power-holder
an unaligned reforming actor benefiting from the fallout

rows.need: a single formal contest must support more than two outcome tiers, each with a categorically different consequence set, not merely a scaled version of the same consequence
the institution's best possible outcome must remove a suppression effect the target was providing against a background pressure quantity, and immediately spike that quantity
a failed formal challenge against a power-holder must weaken the challenging institution and strengthen the target correspondingly, not simply leave the state unchanged

crossing an accumulating threshold on the spiking background quantity must trigger an automatic, self-sustaining escalation procedure that continues running each period without further single decisions
a target who repels the accusation must be able to leverage held evidence of a separate misconduct by the institution to open a counter-offensive
reversing a wrongly-decided formal judgment must require its own separate, high-cost formal procedure rather than a simple appeal

ARC-22.name: The Ceiral Ritual
ARC-22.one_line: An irreversible, prerequisite-gated one-time ritual, reachable only after several independent multi-season preparation tracks converge, must resolve via a graded outcome table that permanently reconfigures a world-level substrate condition differently at each degree.
ARC-22.ends_when: never fully -- an Overwhelming result triggers an endgame-level structural change; any other degree leaves the operation re-attemptable, so it 'ends' only when a permanent-tier outcome is reached or the players give up
who_acts: the lead practitioner (undergoing the roll)
the assembled supporting participants
the faction leader whose personal transformation and political leverage depend on the outcome
a scholarly figure whose own independent long-running track intersects with the event's visibility

rows.need: several independent long-running preparation tracks (a held object, a regional awareness value, a qualified lead individual, assembled qualified participants) must all reach specific thresholds simultaneously before the operation becomes available at all
the lead individual attempting the operation must have their own separate loyalty/alignment status materially affect the attempt, complicating what would otherwise be a pure mechanical roll
the operation must resolve via one roll with at least four discrete outcome degrees, each producing a categorically different persistent world-state

the worst outcome degree must spawn a persistent hostile presence that must itself be resolved through several different possible methods before the operation can be reattempted, and must remove the prior lead from being able to try again

the best outcome must permanently change what a specific location can be used for, and must cascade into other characters' independently-tracked knowledge/development thresholds becoming newly reachable
the failure outcome's substrate damage must interact with a pre-existing local weak point to make future failures of the same type more likely nearby

ARC-23.name: The General Falls
ARC-23.one_line: [STRUCK-MECHANIC: Coup Counter] A mass-combat commander's incapacitation must escalate through two stages tied to a single narrow-window rescue action, and her death must silently and permanently delete a separate standing threat that existed only because she personally maintained it.
ARC-23.ends_when: the battle resolves and its immediate command-state consequence is set (recovered, uncommanded rout, capture, or death) -- a natural single-scene end; the aftermath vacuum is a separate, open-ended consequence
who_acts: the commander (whose earlier decision to commit forces set up this crisis)
any character with the relevant rescue skill (attempting stabilization)
the opposing force's leader (choosing to kill or capture on victory)

rows.need: a battle must have discrete resolution phases within a turn, with a stabilization action available only in one particular phase and only for a single turn's window
whether any character has invested in a specific, rarely-used skill area chosen at character creation (not in this scene) must gate whether the stabilization attempt can be made at all
a commander's incapacitation must impose an immediate structural penalty on the entire force's collective effectiveness and remove a stabilizing floor on morale, not just remove one combatant
failing to stabilize must escalate to a second, worse stage on the following turn, removing command capacity from the whole force rather than only worsening the commander's own state
a standing threat/threshold that exists only because one specific person personally maintains it must be permanently extinguished -- not paused, not inherited by a successor -- if that person dies
an opposing force defeating a leader in combat must be able to choose capture over death, creating a distinct ongoing leverage/hostage state different from either party surviving normally or dying

ARC-24.name: The Faction That Breaks
ARC-24.one_line: An institution's health quantity hitting zero must trigger a structural fracture into distinct successor entities, with the fracture's exact shape depending on unrelated sub-actors' independent states at the moment of collapse.
ARC-24.ends_when: never universally -- political-vacuum branches stabilize, reconstruction branches complete, or the frozen quantity later triggers a further cascade; no single terminal condition covers all branches
who_acts: each sub-faction/named figure within the collapsing institution
the players (who may or may not be watching)
rival factions moving into the resulting vacuum

rows.need: an institution's overall health quantity reaching its floor must trigger a structural fracture into multiple independent successor entities, not merely a power reduction
the specific shape of the fracture must depend on the independent internal state of several named sub-actors at the moment of collapse, not on a fixed collapse template
a protective grace mechanism on the health quantity must be able to be missed if the players are not present to use their one available window
a collapsed institution's role in driving a background world-quantity must simply stop rather than reverse, freezing that quantity at whatever value it held
a frozen-but-still-high background quantity must remain crossable by unrelated later events even though the institution that normally drives it is gone, via its own remnant apparatus

rebuilding a collapsed institution from scratch must require multiple geographically-distributed actions gated by the same per-period caps as everything else, fixing a minimum recovery time regardless of investment

ARC-25.name: The Schoenland Pivot
ARC-25.one_line: A self-interested neutral third party must autonomously read the players' domestic state from externally-visible signals alone and choose an alignment that changes a separate escalating pressure's rate, entirely outside player control.
ARC-25.ends_when: never fully -- this is an ongoing background disposition that can flip again; it settles into a durable state only under sustained conditions on either side
who_acts: the neutral third-party actor (autonomous)
Crown/players (trying to present a legible stability signal)
a hostile external power benefiting from the unfavorable pivot

rows.need: a neutral third-party actor must independently evaluate several unrelated background quantities each period and select a strategic alignment based on that composite read, without a player directly setting the alignment
that actor's read must depend only on externally visible signals, such that private mitigations are invisible to it while public/structural events are highly visible
the chosen alignment must change the ongoing rate of a separate, unrelated escalating pressure quantity on one path, and open automatic passive intelligence leakage to a hostile power on the other
the intelligence-leakage side effect must run passively and automatically regardless of player awareness, exposing covert operations run through that territory
locking in the favorable alignment must require meeting several externally-visible qualifying conditions simultaneously, not any single action
the third party's default disposition must remain profit-seeking/neutral even under alignment, able to pull back into self-interest rather than becoming a committed ally or true enemy

ARC-26.name: The Duke Awakens
ARC-26.one_line: A background quantity accumulates invisibly on an NPC from his own routine actions and, on crossing a threshold, triggers a one-time check whose result permanently and irreversibly reforges his capabilities and worldview.
ARC-26.ends_when: never absolutely -- success opens into an ongoing high-level political integration arc; failure opens into an ongoing wrong-framework action arc that ends only when a subordinate's loyalty finally breaks or a formal investigation resolves
who_acts: the NPC undergoing the transformation
a second character who already has the capability and chooses silence or disclosure
an institution running an independent detection/investigation process
a subordinate sent on a mission derived from the (possibly false) new belief

rows.need: an NPC's own repeated, self-directed institutional actions must silently accumulate a hidden personal quantity that the character himself is unaware of

crossing a threshold on that hidden quantity must trigger a one-time check whose two outcomes are qualitatively different: a true capability unlocked, versus a false self-generated belief acted on with full resources

the failure branch must produce behavior that is objectively counter-productive to the character's own interests while looking, to him, like the correct reading of his experience -- and must remain actable-upon with his full institutional resources

a second character who already possesses the same capability must be able to independently perceive the first character's growth and choose whether to disclose it, driven by a personal conflict-of-interest rather than a scripted trigger
the newly-unlocked capability must retroactively change how the character interprets and leverages his existing political relationships and leverage, not simply add a new resource

an institution that would normally react to this kind of capability must be able to open a formal investigation based on partial/indirect evidence before the character himself understands what has happened to him

ARC-27.name: The Dissolution
ARC-27.one_line: A single risky reality-altering operation must resolve via a graded outcome table where even the best result carries an unavoidable exposure side effect, and the worst result produces an immediate, scene-local hostile manifestation whose severity depends on ambient world-health at the moment of the attempt.
ARC-27.ends_when: the operation resolves in one roll -- a single-scene event; a Partial-outcome sub-arc ends when the unstable condition is mended or deteriorates into the worst case
who_acts: the acting practitioner (choosing to attempt it and the target)
allies who must respond if a hostile manifestation fires
sensitive observers in the scene, whose mere presence has consequences

rows.need: a single declared operation must resolve to at least four distinct outcome degrees, each combining differently whether the target is removed, whether a persistent breach forms, whether the actor is incapacitated, and how much a world-health quantity is spent

even the best possible outcome must produce a passive detection/visibility effect for sufficiently sensitive observers physically present, with a political consequence firing regardless of whether the primary goal succeeded
the worst outcome must spawn a hostile entity in the exact physical/social scene where the operation was attempted, with its type determined by what was targeted and at what scale

the ambient world-health quantity's pre-existing band must change what a bad outcome does next -- the same numeric penalty must cross into a qualitatively worse global band if the ambient quantity was already low, or be absorbed if it was high
an intermediate outcome must leave an unstable, still-active anomalous condition that deteriorates into the worst case after a fixed delay unless separately, deliberately addressed
removing a physical record via this operation must not remove the corresponding knowledge already held in people's minds

ARC-28.name: Vaynard -- The Reckoner Who Saw the Sum
ARC-28.one_line: A character's internal capability-cost quantity reaching its floor must be a permanent, non-fatal transformation that keeps him playable and his goals intact while categorically changing what he can understand and communicate.
ARC-28.ends_when: never -- this is a durable state that persists for the remainder of the campaign; it has no closing condition of its own
who_acts: the transformed character himself (choosing physical transformation or not, and how to shape each communication)
the players (choosing to trust and act on unverifiable advice)
his practitioner ally

rows.need: a character's internal capability-cost quantity must be able to reach its floor not as death or incapacitation but as a permanent qualitative transformation that keeps him alive, coherent, and goal-continuous

after crossing that threshold, the character's communication to others must be deliberately down-sampled per-listener -- the same true information rendered differently and incompletely depending on who receives it, controlled by the transformed character himself

the transformed character must retain full continuity of prior goals, relationships, and decision framework, so others recognize him as unchanged in identity while being unable to independently verify his now-superior judgments
the transformed character must face a further, independent choice about whether to also alter his physical form, decoupled from the mental-threshold crossing itself
if the character holds ongoing political leverage, its meaning must be reinterpretable at a deeper level after the threshold without changing its face value to those who negotiated it originally

ARC-29.name: Almud -- The King at the Limit of Order
ARC-29.one_line: A reigning head of state crossing the same internal transformation threshold as Arc 28 must be able to either continue formally occupying his role at reduced legibility, or voluntarily vacate it, immediately triggering ordinary succession machinery.
ARC-29.ends_when: Branch A never ends within this arc (the reign continues); Branch B ends the moment he formally vacates the throne, which is itself the trigger for a separate succession process outside this arc's scope
who_acts: the head of state himself (choosing to remain or step down)
the institutional military leader deciding whether to escalate against him
the players (interacting with him post-threshold)

rows.need: a formal head-of-state role must be able to be voluntarily vacated by its holder as a deliberate act distinct from death, incapacity, or removal, immediately triggering the normal succession process

a head of state who remains in his role after crossing the transformation threshold must retain the ability to perform ordinary formal governance acts (signing decrees, attending formal sessions) even while his understanding of them has changed underneath

a watching institutional actor with her own private judgment threshold must be able to treat a single conversation with the transformed head of state as sufficient answer to stand down from an escalating institutional action, without that being a scripted persuasion roll

two independently-transformed characters occupying the same physical space must be able to communicate with each other at full fidelity, distinct from their now-limited communication with everyone else

ARC-30.name: Lenneth -- What She Finally Understood
ARC-30.one_line: A long-concealed secret capability crossing the Arc 28/29 transformation threshold must remain undetectable to non-specialist observers even afterward, with discovery gated specifically on one particular relationship rather than general exposure risk.
ARC-30.ends_when: never as background state; the discovery sub-arc ends at the discovery scene itself; a further political-action sub-arc ends when the act she was building toward is finally taken
who_acts: the transformed character (maintaining concealment, funding networks, and shaping disclosure)
the discovering relational partner (if/when discovery occurs)
the players (interacting with her before or after discovery)

rows.need: a long-concealed identity/capability must remain undetectable to non-specialist observers even after a profound internal transformation, requiring concealment to be tracked independently of the internal-state change

covert funding/support networks the character has been running must continue operating after the threshold, but their guiding logic must shift from strategic calculation to something the operator herself describes as direct perception, without changing their external behavior enough to raise suspicion

discovery of the transformation by one specific, relationally-close character must produce a fundamentally different scene depending on whether that discoverer has independently crossed the same threshold himself

a physical object with historical/informational significance must be able to carry a perceivable proximity relationship to a transformed character that is legible only to sufficiently sensitive observers

ARC-31.name: The Quaestio of Baralta
ARC-31.one_line: [STRUCK-MECHANIC: Coup Counter (Loewenritter Autonomy) and Niflhel/covert intelligence network -- both explicitly retired by the source file's own note] A formal high-stakes tribunal between an institution and a challenger must be interruptible mid-proceeding by an unrelated covert faction's violent action, penalizing whoever was mid-turn, with the eventual verdict both shifting a background quantity and silently incrementing a fourth party's private, unshared threshold.
ARC-31.ends_when: the tribunal resolves and its immediate consequence fires; the arc as a whole has no single end -- it hands off into either de-escalation or a mass battle whose resolution is a separate, unposed question
who_acts: the challenger (formal accuser)
the institution's leadership
the covert intelligence faction
the watching military leader (private judgment)
her opposing commander in the eventual battle

rows.need: a formal, multi-exchange debate procedure must be interruptible by an out-of-genre violent event originating from an unrelated third faction, imposing a resource/strain penalty on whoever was mid-exchange when it hit

the tribunal's win/lose outcome for the challenger must apply a categorically different consequence pair depending on which side wins -- one side's win drops an institutional pressure quantity, the other's win raises it and also silently increments a separate private counter held by an uninvolved fourth party

a private, unshared threshold maintained by one specific NPC (not by the institution she serves) must be able to trigger an institution-scale event once it reaches its ceiling, based on her own accumulated judgment rather than any single rule anyone else can see

a covert intelligence-gathering faction operating through a proxy network must be able to attempt a targeted lethal action against a person inside a formal, non-combat social scene, with success or failure both producing distinct downstream consequences for that faction's own standing
an institutional actor's positioned military forces must be able to remain ambiguous in intent (defensive vs threatening) until a later decision point forces an interpretation

ARC-32.name: Vaynard's Confession
ARC-32.one_line: A faction leader's private, invisible knowledge-accumulation track and a separate institutional surveillance track, built from unrelated events, must be able to reach their thresholds in the same window and converge on the same target -- the leader's ally -- without either side of the convergence knowing about the other.
ARC-32.ends_when: the tribunal/vote resolves and the accused's fate is set -- a definite conclusion, though the leader's own trajectory continues open-ended afterward
who_acts: the faction leader (unaware of his own transformation)
the ally performing the triggering action
the surveillance institution's investigator
a formal deliberative body
a second unrelated NPC whose independent threshold also fires

rows.need: a faction leader's private capability track must reach a threshold via ordinary relationship-building actions, and on threshold must trigger a resolvable moment that fires on an ALLY's action performed on the leader's behalf, not on the leader's own action

an institutional surveillance track targeting a specific individual must accumulate independently from unrelated prior encounters and reach its own threshold in the same window as the leader's private track, without either track's owner aware of the other

a formal collective decision body must be able to intervene to defend or abandon an accused individual via a multi-round contest, with the losing side's consequence being a fully asymmetric tribunal with no defense procedure available

a second, unrelated NPC's own slow-building threshold, running as background 'processing the archive' activity, must be able to fire its own check in the middle of the tribunal proceeding, adding a third independent thread to the convergence

the accused individual's fate on conviction must branch hard, with severity depending on a separate quantity elsewhere in the world (whether it is currently safe for them there), rather than being self-contained to this arc

ARC-33.name: The Forgetting Road
ARC-33.one_line: An expedition into a zone that actively strips participants' recall of their own goal must still let them bring back a non-verbal, embodied change, and that change must be automatically detectable by a hostile institution the instant it becomes visible, regardless of any subsequent player action.
ARC-33.ends_when: the post-return cascade resolves -- sanctuary holds and the investigation stalls, or the battle resolves and a long-term substrate-management cycle begins or fails to begin
who_acts: the expedition members (choosing to enter and what to do inside)
the institutional investigator (running an independent background process)
the sheltering faction's leader (deciding whether to protect)
that faction's military commander (in the mass-combat branch)

rows.need: a location must be able to strip a person's explicit recall of their specific goal while inside it, while still letting them retain and act on the underlying intention, such that 'why am I here' becomes unanswerable moment to moment while 'what to do next' remains actionable

knowledge or procedure gained inside such a memory-stripping zone must be able to be carried home in participants' own configuration rather than in an external record, surviving the strip in a form other than explicit recall

a successful, player-desired outcome achieved via this zone must trigger an automatic, unavoidable rise in a hostile institution's background pressure quantity purely because the outcome became visible, independent of any subsequent handling

an institutional surveillance track built from unrelated prior background activity must independently reach its own threshold around the same time and open a formal investigation of the returnees, without coordination with the automatic pressure spike above

a third-party faction offering protection must be able to contest the resulting investigation via a faction-scale action whose success depends on that faction's own independently-tracked standing, not a fixed difficulty set for this arc
if sanctuary fails or is declined, the conflict must escalate to a formal mass-combat engagement whose outcome alters the same background pressure quantity again, in either direction

ARC-34.name: Ehrenwall's Count
ARC-34.one_line: [STRUCK-MECHANIC: Coup Counter (Loewenritter Autonomy) -- explicitly retired by the source file's own note; also cites Niflhel] Three structurally independent threshold-crossings from three unrelated systems must each be able to increment the same private, never-decrementing counter, whose ceiling issues a formal ultimatum resolved through the ordinary civic debate mechanism under threat of force.
ARC-34.ends_when: the confrontation resolves -- the debate removes the emergency-powers state, or the subsequent battle resolves -- either terminates this arc, though the broader question of what kind of state this is remains open by design
who_acts: the counter-holder (autonomous, private judgment, never decrementing)
the head of state (refusing or complying with the ultimatum)
each faction responding to the emergency-powers state per its own tolerance for covert operation
an external power reacting to the outcome

rows.need: a private, monotonically-increasing counter held by a single actor must be incrementable by at least three structurally unrelated trigger conditions, such that none of the three 'knows' about the others
that counter reaching its ceiling must issue a formal ultimatum to the current head of state (cede a specific authority or face an emergency-powers action) rather than an immediate seizure of power
refusal of the ultimatum must trigger an emergency-powers state applying uniformly across a whole territory, imposing extra friction on non-approved actors everywhere in it simultaneously

the emergency-powers state must be revocable through the same formal civic debate mechanism as ordinary politics, whose failure must itself trigger further external escalation rather than simply maintaining the status quo

whether the counter's holder enforces her position at the resulting confrontation must be resolvable via a mass-combat engagement whose outcome retroactively validates or invalidates the deposed authority's legitimacy

ARC-35.name: The Klapp Threshold
ARC-35.one_line: A senior institutional scholar's slow, routine research activity must accumulate a hidden exposure quantity that, on threshold, fires a personal-transformation check whose success the institution's own belief system has no accommodating category for, pausing the institution's automatic background power generation until the internal conflict resolves.
ARC-35.ends_when: the internal tribunal resolves (conviction or retention) -- a definite conclusion for this arc, though 'can the institution be reformed from within' is explicitly left open as a broader thread
who_acts: the senior official himself (undergoing transformation, later choosing fracture vs suppression)
the institution's chief investigator (filing internal charges)
the institution's presiding leader (torn between doctrine and capability)
an external faction quietly benefiting from covert leaks

rows.need: a senior official's long, routine, in-role activity must be trackable as a slow-accumulating hidden exposure quantity over multiple seasons that eventually crosses a threshold and fires a one-time check, purely as a side effect of doing his normal job

that check's success must produce a genuinely destabilizing personal transformation in a senior official whose institution's belief system treats the transformation as forbidden or unclassifiable, forcing a choice between doctrine and his continued institutional value

an internal leadership crisis inside an institution, invisible to outside political bodies, must be able to pause that institution's automatic passive background power generation for as long as the crisis is unresolved

the institution must be able to formally try its own senior official via an asymmetric internal tribunal with no defense procedure, where conviction removes him but restores paused generation, and non-conviction keeps him at the cost of ongoing instability

if retained, the transformed official must be able to become a covert asset feeding capability to an external actor the institution formally opposes, while the institution's internal factional split persists as an ongoing unresolved background condition

ARC-36.name: The Tithe That Fed the Enemy
ARC-36.one_line: An institution's internally-consistent resource-optimization behavior must be able to systematically erode a separate, unmeasured cultural-trust resource in exactly the territories where it is heaviest, forming a structural trap with no equilibrium that no single actor's viewpoint spans.
ARC-36.ends_when: never cleanly -- the loop has no equilibrium and resolves only via removing the optimizing official, or by his complete, uncontested success; both are structural end-conditions, not calendar dates
who_acts: the institution's resource-optimizing official
the institution's investigative official (constrained by procedure)
the opposing cultural movement's organizer (spreading opportunistically)
affected communities (whose sentiment is the eroding resource)

rows.need: an NPC pursuing a fixed optimization objective must be able to keep taking the locally-correct action indefinitely with no internal signal that a completely different, unmeasured value is being destroyed by that same behavior
a slow-eroding, per-location cultural/loyalty value must silently accumulate downward from resource extraction, invisible until an opposing movement's presence becomes visible as a lagging indicator

an institution's investigative branch, on detecting the derivative marker, must apply a procedure that structurally cannot address the actual root cause because that cause belongs to a different category of problem than the procedure is built to find
the investigating branch's standard procedural delay must itself allow the underlying erosion to continue and spread to additional locations during the investigation
the eroding value crossing a floor in enough locations simultaneously must trigger a discrete, disruptive event with its own immediate costs, distinct from the slow erosion that caused it
this arc's terminal event must be able to feed as an input into other independently-running arcs' state without requiring any player action to connect them

ARC-37.name: The Heresy in the Warehouse
ARC-37.one_line: [STRUCK-MECHANIC: Niflhel trade network] A mundane supply chain built by two non-perceiving actors must secretly carry a categorically hazardous good invisible below a rare sensory threshold, and two separate investigators perceiving only one dimension each must be able to converge on the same target without either knowing about the other.
ARC-37.ends_when: the exposure event fires (or is suppressed) -- a definite conclusion for the immediate arc, with downstream consequences continuing into other arcs
who_acts: two independent supply-chain operators (neither perceiving the hazard)
the rare accidental discoverer (self-protective)
her own chain of command (auditing her pattern, not the secret)
a second, unrelated investigator (provenance-based)
a hostile institution deciding whether to prosecute

rows.need: a legitimate, ordinary supply chain must carry a good whose hazardous property is invisible to everyone below a specific rare perceptual threshold, such that its builders and vendors are neither lying nor negligent

a rare individual who crosses the perceptual threshold and encounters the hidden property incidentally, while doing an unrelated job, must have a personal behavioral reason to avoid reporting it, generating an accumulating cost to herself rather than resolving immediately

that accumulating self-protective cost must itself be observable from outside by the discoverer's own chain of command as an unexplained pattern, eventually forcing an internal review independent of the underlying secret

a separate investigator working an unrelated case must be able to cross-reference unconnected case files and stumble onto the same supply chain from a different angle, using only legally-visible evidence rather than the hidden property

when the legally-visible investigation concludes against the supply chain, it must automatically hand a hostile institution a costless, pre-built justification to open its own separate, harsher investigation
exposure of the supply chain must be able to propagate damage to at least three separate actors' standing via three distinct causal paths from one triggering event

ARC-38.name: The Sandcastle Alliance

Her personal sympathy for a population she is ordered to act against must produce a measurable, repeatable delay or softening in her actions against that population, distinct from a single one-time refusal.

An office must be able to be the sole official channel between an institution and an entire class of informal, deniable actors, such that removing that one office-holder severs the institution's access rather than merely weakening it.

A person's private, undisclosed heritage or sympathy must be able to bias which of her discoveries she reports faithfully and which she quietly softens or withholds, without the player or her principal being able to verify, in any single instance, which she did.
The office must be able to continue functioning (brokered deals still resolving, information still flowing) across a season in which the player takes no action involving her at all.

Each administrative action must be resolvable by more than one method, where the choice of method hands durable influence over the settlement to a different internal faction, rather than the raw magnitude of the action being the only thing that changes.

The governor's controlling authority must be able to issue a mandatory seasonal order she can comply with, negotiate down, or defy -- each option costing something different to the authority above versus the populace below -- with repeated defiance accumulating toward a threshold that eventually forces a reckoning.

Named local actors under a governor's authority must be able to want incompatible things from EACH OTHER (not just from her), so that resolving one actor's grievance necessarily worsens another's, independent of any single choice she makes.

The same office-holder must simultaneously make one specific class of routine, stabilizing action easier or faster to accomplish, as the compensating flip side of the reform tax.

An office-holder must be able to hold institutional memory -- exact knowledge of an original founding agreement's terms -- that no other living actor holds, such that a proposal to alter those terms can be checked only against a standard nobody else can independently verify.
