This office-holder must be able to remain a purely institutional, non-directly-playable modifier under ordinary conditions, and only become a personally-acting, decision-making NPC once the institution falls below a stability threshold.

An office-holder must be able to take a repeatable seasonal action that reliably improves one faction-wide resource, with the improvement scaling by how many subordinate territories the office applies it to.

Sustained harm from this office-holder's pattern in a given locality must be able to accumulate toward a distinct, nameable crisis event, rather than simply continuing to degrade a number indefinitely.

A player character must be able to intervene directly in this office-holder's tithe-collection pattern in one specific territory, altering the outcome there without requiring institutional authority over the Cardinal himself.

A faction representative must be able to repeatedly grow one faction stat at the direct, automatic expense of a second faction stat every season, as her default behavior rather than a one-time choice offered to the player.

An economic actor's supply chain must be able to carry a hidden property that she has no way to detect given her own perceptual limits, such that she is materially responsible for a consequence she is structurally incapable of becoming aware of through her own effort.

A person must be able to hold two distinct organizational offices at once -- a cross-faction liaison seat and a rank within her home institution's own ladder -- each with its own advancement conditions, usable somewhat independently.

A formal institutional gate she benefits from (an examination or credentialing process) must be able to carry a procedural, plausibly-deniable bias against a specific population, so that individual gatekeepers can point to 'the rules' rather than to her personal order, while she still benefits from the aggregate effect.

An advisor whose sole articulated commitment is precedent and consistency must have every persuasive approach toward her scored differently depending on whether it appeals to established rule or to ad hoc circumstance, with the ad hoc approach yielding systematically less even when otherwise persuasive.

A person embedded in one institution's inner circle must be able to be the single necessary formal conduit through which a SECOND institution's authority -- to which he actually answers -- can legally act inside the first institution's territory; without him, that authority does not exist there procedurally.

The institution he is embedded in must be able to refuse the request he is required to make on his true institution's behalf, under a specific named condition, so that his advocacy can fail even when he performs his function correctly.

A third party must be able to discover which of his two loyalties actually governed a specific past action of his, and that discovery must damage his standing in the institution he was seen to have subordinated, without necessarily being provable to the institution he was actually protecting.
The leader must be able to formally and publicly recognize another person's deed in a way that changes what that person may subsequently do, and this recognition must be withholdable, not automatic.

A crisis inside the leader's own family (an heir's death, a spouse's death, an heir's capture) must be able to fire unpredictably and reconfigure what the leader does for many subsequent seasons, visibly to every other actor.

A third party's multi-season campaign to eventually replace the leader must be able to proceed in parallel to his reign without the leader having any action that ends it outright, only ones that slow or manage it.

A future succession must be able to remain genuinely unsettled for the leader's whole reign, contested among parties with different bases of claim, none of which the leader can fully foreclose by simply naming an heir.
A religious institution's supreme leader must be able to publicly rule on doctrine in a way that materially shifts political-military measures elsewhere on the board.

The leader must be able to face a decision where every theologically coherent answer available to him damages the institution in a different way, so there is no clean resolution regardless of which he picks.

The leader must be able to delegate separate domains of institutional power (military, judicial, economic, scholarly) to different subordinate leaders who can each independently drift from his control, up to becoming more dangerous than he was.
A person's capacity for a certain kind of perception must be able to be permanently foreclosed by their institutional belief system, reachable again only through a shock external to ordinary play.

A leader must be able to build a multi-season positioning campaign toward a higher seat that only becomes attemptable once specific external conditions — the target seat's weakness AND a general instability threshold — are simultaneously true, so years of preparation can sit inert waiting on someone else's failure.

A claimant's success at seizing the higher seat must be conditioned on a third party's institutional state at the exact moment of the claim, so that an early, a middle, and a late attempt in the same campaign produce categorically different outcomes.

Taking the higher seat must be able to threaten the fracture of the claimant's home institution, contingent on a separate instability measure that keeps accumulating whether or not she is paying attention to it.

A leader who governs entirely through legalistic, precedent-bound methods must be able to become willing to act outside those methods once a specific named institutional failure occurs, and that shift must persist rather than reset the following season.

A theological or ideological innovation a leader personally originates must be able to spread its effects across the population she governs on a timescale much longer than the campaign, so it can exist as true worldbuilding without being an active mechanical variable.

A leader must be able to declare that no other party, including his own institution, can be trusted with the thing he protects, and act on that declaration in a way that isolates him from natural allies pursuing the same outcome.

An ideologically aligned peer with institutional access this leader lacks must be able to refuse to accelerate a shared goal on his preferred timeline, so agreement on diagnosis does not guarantee cooperation on method or pace.
A non-military, non-secret means of contesting a territory's cultural or religious alignment must be able to shift that alignment without transferring who controls the territory.

The military leader assessing the ruler must be able to hold and act on a private professional judgment that is never voiced to the ruler as an accusation, yet still accumulates mechanically over time.
A diplomatic action by an outside party must be able to persuade the military institution to change its deployment posture without going through the ruler at all.

A person recognized as a movement's leader must be able to exert real influence and be targeted by opponents before any formal institutional seat or organizational structure exists for the movement at all, with that authority measured through relational and reputational quantities rather than a rank she occupies.

A leader must be able to choose, season after season, between consolidating her base in fewer places or spreading it thinly across many, with that choice producing a measurably different vulnerability to a specific opposing institution's enforcement action.

A local population must be able to unilaterally shift its own governance to this movement's control the moment its existing governance completely collapses, without the movement's central leadership needing to have taken any action there that season.

An external, unpredictable event unrelated to this person's own choices must be able to instantly convert her from an influence-only actor into the sole holder of supreme authority, with every downstream political relationship reconfiguring around the change in the same event.

Ascending to supreme authority through this path must be able to instantly and permanently redefine what the ruling institution stands for, flipping an ambient, privately-held policy uncertainty into an explicit, declared doctrine, rather than merely changing which person occupies the seat.

A minor heir's declared loyalty must be able to transfer wholesale from one guardian to another the moment the first guardian is removed, without requiring the heir's own independent choice in that moment.

A minor political heir must be able to start with no fixed ideological alignment, such that his eventual alignment is determined by which external party successfully builds a relationship with him first, within a bounded time window.

The heir's maturation from a dependent status into an independent political actor with his own agenda must be able to be triggered by any of several different kinds of event — elapsed time, his own accumulated preparation, a crisis in the ruling institution, or the current ruler's death — whichever comes first.

A slow institutional-pressure measure driven by concern for this person's safety must be able to convert instantly into an acute crisis the moment she is credibly endangered, rather than scaling continuously.

This person's return to her home polity must be conditioned entirely on an unrelated family member's death via an unpredictable event, and that return must require an active operation into hostile third-party territory rather than a simple diplomatic recall.

If this person is eventually returned home and made politically relevant, her formative external upbringing must be able to shape how her political identity subsequently develops, distinct from how a home-raised heir's identity develops.

The single most capable person in a specialized domain must be structurally unable to communicate her work's urgency to anyone who cannot already perceive what she perceives, regardless of how clearly or urgently she tries.

This character must be able to operate entirely outside any faction's institutional incentive structure, so no faction can compel, bribe, or politically pressure her the way they can pressure an office-holder.

This character's personal presence must be able to actively worsen the local instability of any place she is forced to travel through, specifically when she has been driven from her post, so her own survival-seeking behavior directly damages the places sheltering her.

This character's personal discipline must be able to let her exceed the normal safety limits that would force anyone else to stop performing a dangerous specialized action, specifically once the surrounding instability crosses a severe threshold.

A party who anticipates this confrontation must be able to preempt it by offering her a specific, falsifiable, time-bound commitment instead, with her willingness to accept scaling by how convincing the offer is, and a real chance the offer is refused outright.

A commitment made to her, once accepted and later fulfilled, must be able to permanently raise her tolerance for future provocation from that specific party, so the relationship is demonstrably and durably different afterward rather than merely reset.

gaps.what: (Person, capability) has no row in the Partition schema
gaps.needs: a social: bool column entry

gaps.what: reserve: nothing marks an act as once-per-arc, nothing records that it is being WITHHELD, and nothing lets its value decay while unused. Holding a hammer is indistinguishable from not having one (and see P19 — the holding itself emits nothing)
gaps.needs: an act kind with a use-once flag and a value that varies with world state, so that waiting is a priced decision rather than an absence

gaps.what: procedural advance: an accusation, a probate, a licence application — a process with STAGES that advance on their own timetable — has no carrier. A Record is inert (A9 shows even its ttl is never decremented), and CALENDAR fires dates rather than advancing processes. So a case against you cannot ripen while you do nothing
gaps.needs: a staged Record that MATTER advances, whose stage gates what acts are available

gaps.what: persistent condition: an Event is a fact in the log, not a state on a thing. Nothing carries 'this unit is stuck', 'this person is disgraced', 'this place is under interdict' — a condition that outlives its scene and gates later acts. `09`'s seam returns Events from a contest and stops there
gaps.needs: a condition Record attached to a carrier, with a clearing act — the same shape A16 and P30 need, which is one gap seen three ways

gaps.what: loss of agency: the loop hands EVERY person in `world.persons` to `choose`. There is no state in which a person exists, is lucid, and may no longer choose — so an irreversible personal floor cannot be represented, and the arc that exists BECAUSE the rule has no exit has no rule
gaps.needs: a per-person agency predicate the DELIBERATE map consults, and an act class that can cross it one way only

gaps.what: self-accumulating hidden exposure: the duke performed 5 ordinary acts and the shape retains them ONLY as Events in the world log and as decaying Claims in whoever witnessed them. There is no per-person quantity that (a) climbs from the person's own acts, (b) is NOT readable by that person, and (c) can fire. The nearest thing, the claim ledger, is the wrong shape three ways over: it is other people's, it decays, and its holder reads it
gaps.needs: a monotone interior counter fed by the actor's OWN acts at WITNESS, excluded from that person's own View, with a firing rule that produces an Act by SOMEONE ELSE rather than an outcome — otherwise it is A2's forbidden threshold wearing a hat

gaps.what: contested quantity: both acts resolved and emitted ['restore', 'wreck']; the site's condition took both deltas independently. That is correct for matter and it is NOT contest — nothing in `resolve()` sees that two acts addressed one target in one season, so there is no net, no opposition, and no way for a blocker to hold a line
gaps.where: P35 opposed acts on one target
gaps.needs: either an explicit statement that opposition is emergent from summed deltas and arcs must be written that way, or a resolve() that groups acts by target — the second is a second resolver and the shape's own meta-rule forbids it

gaps.what: action budget: `choose(Person, View, Sensation) -> Act` returns ONE Act, and DELIBERATE called it 1 time(s). A season is one act per person, so nobody triages, nothing is left undone, and a King's scarcity is identical to a copyist's. Note what this also voids: `14` closes the petition-spray defect 'PROVISIONALLY by one act per person', a fix that does not survive the stated player model of ~5
gaps.needs: `choose` returning an ORDERED Act[] bounded by a per-person budget, with the budget itself a Query (office, condition, distance travelled) rather than a constant — and a re-answer to petition-spray that survives a budget above one
